Teaching has been an integral part of my academic career.

My courses are closely connected to my research in information security,
cryptography, digital identity, electronic documents, artificial
intelligence, and the mathematical foundations of computer science.

This section also serves as a long-term archive of lecture notes,
slides, exercises, assignments, and other educational resources
developed throughout my academic career.


## Current Courses

### Mathematical Foundations for Computer Science

Topics include mathematical reasoning, logic, proofs, induction,
recurrences, combinatorics, relations, functions, and other mathematical
foundations used in computer science.

**Level:** Undergraduate

[Course materials →](#)


### Security and Artificial Intelligence

The course investigates the relationship between artificial
intelligence and information security, including the use of AI in
security applications and the security challenges introduced by
AI-based systems and autonomous agents.

**Level:** Undergraduate

[Course materials →](#)


### Security and Usability in Health Information Systems

The course examines security, privacy, usability, identity,
authentication, electronic documents, and trust mechanisms in the
context of health information systems.

**Level:** Graduate

[Course materials →](#)

## Teaching Philosophy

I view teaching and research as closely connected activities.

Students should not only learn established concepts and technologies,
but also understand the problems that motivated them, their limitations,
and the open questions that remain.

In information security and cryptography in particular, this means
combining theoretical foundations with the analysis and construction
of real systems.
